task: Remove the illegal Builder preview to Admin server-action dependency by extracting the existing pilot acceptance start flow into a shared canonical storefront/template acceptance capability without changing acceptance behavior.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The change touches a privileged preview acceptance path that binds a platform operator to a pilot tenant and then redirects into real checkout/runtime flows. The highest proportionate assurance is a behavior-preserving extraction with explicit authority boundaries, server-action contract regression, preview-only and RBAC fail-closed invariants, exact-head tests, typecheck and build. Re-architecting acceptance, authentication or checkout is outside scope.

acceptanceCriteria: The E13 Builder preview no longer imports any module below src/app/admin and imports the canonical pilot acceptance action from its shared authority path.
The previous Admin action module is cleanly replaced: its implementation moves as a Git-detectable rename and every real Admin/test consumer is updated to the shared path.
Preview-only restriction, platform operator authorization, exact pilot tenant validation, role-binding authorization, signed acceptance cookie and flow redirects remain behaviorally unchanged.
No second pilot acceptance engine, token format, tenant resolver or compatibility wrapper is introduced.
invariants: The shared capability remains server-only and requires an authenticated platform operator before creating a pilot acceptance session.
Invalid, missing, unauthorized or non-pilot instance state fails closed through the existing redirect outcomes.
The signed pilot acceptance token continues to be produced only by the canonical pilot-access token authority.
Checkout proof still targets the real shared checkout runtime and does not introduce production mutation.

failureModes: The extraction drops one of the existing authorization or tenant validation branches.
The Admin compatibility wrapper diverges from the shared implementation.
The preview imports the Admin wrapper indirectly and the forbidden dependency survives.
Server-action semantics are lost because the shared function is not exported from a server-action module.
edgeCases: Instance ID is malformed or the pilot instance has no organization.
Role binding is revoked, expired, organization-wide or instance-specific.
Checkout, B2B RFQ and builder flows preserve their existing destinations.

alternatives.summary: Declare Builder to Admin as an allowed authority dependency.
alternatives.reason: That would legalize a presentation/tooling layer calling an Admin action layer and would hide the architectural defect instead of removing it.

alternatives.summary: Move the existing action implementation unchanged to one shared server-action authority and update every real consumer to the new path.
alternatives.reason: A clean rename removes the cross-layer import and lets the existing Reference Sync distinguish code movement from deletion, without wrapper duplication or exceptions.

alternatives.summary: Duplicate a second checkout-proof-specific acceptance action inside the Builder preview.
alternatives.reason: That would create a parallel security-sensitive acceptance authority and violate the single canonical authority invariant.

specialistReviews.finding: The defect is dependency direction, not missing permission for Builder to call Admin.
specialistReviews.resolution: Move the shared capability below both surfaces and keep one implementation owner.

specialistReviews.finding: Extracting an auth-sensitive server action can accidentally weaken preview-only, operator or role-binding checks.
specialistReviews.resolution: Move the existing action body intact under a shared server-action path, retain every fail-closed branch, and update all consumers rather than duplicating or bypassing the checks.

specialistReviews.finding: Next.js form actions require server-action-compatible export semantics.
specialistReviews.resolution: The shared module remains a use-server module and both callers use the same exported async action.

challenge.scenario: The preview keeps importing the old Admin action after extraction.
challenge.finding: The illegal dependency would survive despite a shared helper existing.
challenge.resolution: Regression test forbids any /app/admin/ import from the E13 preview entry.

challenge.scenario: The Admin surface receives a copied implementation instead of a wrapper.
challenge.finding: Two acceptance authorities would immediately diverge.
challenge.resolution: Admin export becomes a thin async delegate to the shared action only.

challenge.scenario: A non-preview environment submits the shared action.
challenge.finding: Acceptance session could become reachable outside its intended environment.
challenge.resolution: Retain the VERCEL_ENV preview-only fail-closed redirect as the first runtime decision.

challenge.scenario: A platform operator lacks a valid owner/admin role binding for the target tenant.
challenge.finding: A signed acceptance cookie must not be issued.
challenge.resolution: Preserve the existing organization/instance role-binding query and allowed predicate before token creation.

challenge.scenario: The shared action changes checkout or B2B RFQ redirect behavior.
challenge.finding: Functional proof or acceptance journeys would silently change.
challenge.resolution: Move redirect branches without semantic edits and assert the expected destinations in regression source checks.

challenge.scenario: The shared module creates its own token or tenant resolver.
challenge.finding: Token/context truth would split across authorities.
challenge.resolution: Continue importing createPilotAcceptanceToken and pilot cookie constants from the canonical pilot-access module.

challenge.scenario: The old lexical Reference Sync interprets an extracted function body as hundreds of deleted implementation expressions.
challenge.finding: A wrapper-plus-copy refactor creates false stale-consumer noise and would require broad exceptions.
challenge.resolution: Use a clean Git-detectable rename of the action implementation and update every real import/source assertion to the new canonical path.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code after widening the file envelope and stop if projected authority or Known Failure scope changes.
Prove Git/Reference Sync sees clean replacement rather than hundreds of removed implementation expressions.
Regression test that E13 preview and Admin acceptance page import the shared action and contain no src/app/admin action dependency.
Update existing source-contract regressions to read the new canonical action path rather than preserve stale location assumptions.
Regression test that shared action retains preview-only, platform-operator, pilot-instance, role-binding, canonical-token and cookie checks.
Run Edit-Time Guard, Incremental Replay, exact-head Quality tests, typecheck, production build and Template Factory gate.

requirements.requirement: Builder preview and Admin acceptance surfaces must import one shared pilot acceptance action, with the old Admin action module removed as a clean replacement.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No runtime or regression consumer may retain the old Admin action module path.

requirements.requirement: The extraction must preserve preview-only, platform operator, pilot-tenant and role-binding authorization before acceptance cookie creation.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Unauthorized or invalid pilot acceptance may not create a signed acceptance session.

requirements.requirement: Admin and Builder callers must share one implementation of the pilot acceptance start flow rather than duplicated logic.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A second pilot acceptance token/session implementation must not be introduced.

notes: Targeted Authority Graph repair transaction. Implementation approach was improved after the legacy Reference Sync correctly blocked a wrapper extraction as apparent code deletion: the final approach is a clean action-file rename with every real consumer updated, no exceptions and no duplicate wrapper. Rebased atomically onto canonical main after #655 Reference Sync rename-export identity fix.
